subject: Deployment residency and preferred mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martínez <s.martinez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Deployment residency and preferred mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — post-call recap

Hi Sofia — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps: 

Call notes: 
- Primary requirement: All patient-identifiable data must remain in the EU (data residency requirement).
- Traffic: mostly EU users, but we have a growing APAC user segment (~10% of traffic) with stricter latency expectations.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + specific audit artifacts; procurement will want an RFI and evidence of KMS/HSM integrations.
- Throughput: estimated ~50 inference requests/sec peak; ~2M tokens/day.

Deployment modes we discussed (high level): 
- Hosted API: fastest to launch; we can pin region routing to EU, but data may traverse other regions for routing/fallback (we can talk routing guarantees).
- Dedicated: reserved EU capacity (SLA, tenancy isolation) — good middle ground for predictable throughput without full Private deployment.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control of network and residency; best for strict legal/regulatory constraints but longer time-to-deploy.

Requested from you: 
1) Can you confirm whether "data must never leave the EU" means: (a) control plane only in EU, or (b) replication, backup and any processing must be EU-only?
2) Would you be open to Dedicated capacity hosted in our EU region if we can provide contractual residency clauses and KMS-integrated key control?
3) Please share the procurement/RFI doc when convenient — I attached our short RFI template (stub).

Next steps I propose: 1) technical deep-dive with Rishi/Dev to validate latency and topology (I'll schedule), 2) send compliance artifacts (SOC2, encryption details), 3) provide pricing ballpark for Dedicated vs Private options.

Attachments: [attachment: Acme_RFI.docx] (you can drop edits there).

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa

From: Sofia Martínez <s.martinez@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment residency and preferred mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — post-call follow-up

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from procurement & security: 

1) "EU-only" requirement: our legal team expects that all customer data (including backups and analytics derived from PII) must be stored and processed only within EU jurisdictions. Control-plane metadata that does not include customer PII is OK in the US but we prefer it in the EU where possible.

2) KMS: we need customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) and HSM-backed keys for production — is that supported in Hosted/Dedicated?

3) Cross-region routing: for APAC users we want low-latency inference. If we route APAC requests to an EU-hosted Dedicated cluster, acceptable latency is up to 300ms; ideally we would have a hybrid approach (EU data residency + edge inference for APAC non-PII Tier). Can Redwood support split-routing or model variants pinned to regions?

4) Timeline: procurement would like initial pricing and the RFI answers by EOD next week (2026-03-22) so they can include it in the Q2 procurement packet. Target deployment window is Q3.

I've attached the RFI our procurement team started.

—Sofia
Sofia Martínez
Head of Platform Integrations, Acme Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martínez <s.martinez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T15:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Deployment residency and preferred mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — answers & next steps

Sofia — thanks for the clear asks, very helpful. Answers inline: 

1) EU residency scope: we can support EU-only storage & processing for all customer PII including backups and analytics when you choose Dedicated or Private deployment. For Hosted API we support EU-region routing and storage, but certain control-plane metadata may reside outside EU unless contractually restricted. If you require strict contractual residency for everything, Dedicated (with contractual residency clauses) or Private VPC is the recommended path.

2) KMS/BYOK: supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted API supports customer-managed keys via bring-your-own-key for encryption at rest in our EU region, but HSM-backed customer key custody for Hosted is limited — for HSM-backed keys we recommend Dedicated with KMS integration or Private where you run your own key store.

3) Cross-region routing / hybrid topology: we support split-routing policies — requests can be routed by region, cost tier, or SLA. Two patterns we typically recommend: 
   - Primary EU Dedicated cluster for all PII + controlled fallbacks to other regions for non-PII inference.
   - Dedicated EU for PII + lightweight APAC edge nodes running a redacted model variant for latency-sensitive, non-PII traffic.
Latency: we can run an initial perf check in our APAC region and provide measured p95 numbers for your payload in the tech deep-dive.

4) Timeline & deliverables: we'll provide a pricing ballpark, a Dedicated vs Private comparison doc, and the compliance artifacts (SOC2, encryption notes, KMS integration guide) by 2026-03-22. Rishi and Dev will own the tech deep-dive and perf tests.

Attachments for your review: [attachment: Redwood_Dedicated_Overview.pdf], [attachment: Data_Residency_FAQ.docx].

Proposed next step: 60-minute technical deep-dive w/ Rishi & Dev next week — are you available 2026-03-18 or 03-19 (EU morning / our afternoon)?

Best,
Marissa

Rishi / Dev — quick internal summary and asks before the technical call: 

Summary: Acme Health requires EU-only residency for PII including backups/analytics. They have ~50 req/s peak, ~2M tokens/day. APAC users (~10%) need lower latency; proposal is EU Dedicated for PII and APAC edge for non-PII inference or a hybrid approach. Procurement wants RFI answers and pricing by 2026-03-22. Target deployment Q3.

Asks: 
- Rishi: can you prepare a short perf plan and confirm whether an EU Dedicated cluster can handle 50 req/s with p95 latency target <200ms for their payload. Also include estimates for cost of reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go.
- Dev: please prepare notes on KMS/HSM options across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, any caveats for Hosted BYOK in EU, and steps required for Private VPC onboarding (approx. lead time).

I'll coordinate scheduling with Sofia once you confirm availability 03-18 or 03-19. I'll attach the two docs I just sent to Acme in the HubSpot record.

—Marissa
